# API Certificate Authentication

Use an API certificate downloaded as a PKCS#12 bundle for mTLS authentication.
The provider requires the absolute file path and reads its password only from
`VES_P12_PASSWORD`. There is no `api_p12_password` provider argument.

## Step 1: Create Credentials

Follow [Generate API Certificate for My Credentials](https://flatrender.tora.reviews/docs-v2/administration/how-tos/user-mgmt/Credentials#generate-api-certificate-for-my-credentials)
to create and download the certificate.

## Step 2: Set Environment Variables

Use environment variables for both the API-certificate bundle path and its
password. The provider block can then omit credentials:

```sh
export F5XCProvider_URL="https://<tenant>.console.ves.volterra.io/api"
export F5XCProvider_API_P12_FILE="/secure/path/api-credential.p12"
export VES_P12_PASSWORD="<p12-password>"
```

```terraform
provider "f5xc" {}
```

Alternatively, configure the API-certificate bundle path in the provider block.
The password must still be supplied through `VES_P12_PASSWORD`:

```terraform
provider "f5xc" {
  url          = "https://<tenant>.console.ves.volterra.io/api"
  api_p12_file = "/secure/path/api-credential.p12"
}
```

## Step 3: Test Namespace Creation

Create a namespace to verify the provider can authenticate to F5 XC:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    f5xc = {
      source = "F5Networks/f5xc"
    }
  }
}

resource "f5xc_namespace" "authentication_test" {
  name        = "terraform-auth-test"
  description = "Created to verify API certificate authentication."
}
```

Do not combine an API certificate with an API token. Inject the password at
runtime from a CI/CD secret manager and do not commit the bundle or password to
source control.

Return to the [authentication overview](authentication.md).
